Rashi on Yevamot 54a:10:1.english: To press against a wall - He does not intend [it] for the sake of sexual intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:12:1.hebrew: שכן מטמאה את בועלה - להיות כמותה טמא ז', דכתיב: "ותהי נדתה עליו וטמא שבעת ימים" (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ד):
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:12:1.english: In that she renders the one who has intercourse with her ritually impure - to be ritually impure like her for seven [days], as it is written: "And her menstrual impurity shall be upon him, and he shall be impure for seven days" (Leviticus 15:24).

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:13:1.english: And is his brother's wife always a niddah - And does she not cease [menstruating]?

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:14:1.english: For it is within his power - [That is, the power] of a person to increase many women [forbidden] to his brother under the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:14:2.hebrew: דאי בעי מקדש ואזיל כי אלפא - ותפשוט מינה כל עריות הנאסרות עליו מחמת אישות, כגון אשת אב וכלתו וחמותו ואחות אשתו; אבל אמו ואחותו ובתו וכיוצא בהן, דאין בידו לרבות, מנלן:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:14:2.english: As, if he wishes, he can go on betrothing a thousand [women] - And [from this] you may derive all forbidden relatives that become forbidden to him on account of marriage, such as a father's wife, his daughter-in-law, his mother-in-law, and his wife's sister; however, [as for] his mother, his sister, his daughter, and the like, where it is not in his power to increase [their number], from where [do we derive them]?

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:15:1.hebrew: שכן איסור הבא מאליו - ופשוט מינה אמו ואחותו ובתו וכיוצא בהן, ולא תפשוט מינה עריות הנאסרות לו מחמת קידושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:15:1.english: For [it is] a prohibition that comes on its own - And [thus] you may derive from it his mother, his sister, his daughter, and the like, but you cannot derive from it forbidden relatives who are prohibited to him on account of betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:16:1.hebrew: מאשת אח ואחות אב ואם - דכי פרכת: מה לאחות אב ואם, שכן איסור הבא מאליו? אשת אח תוכיח. מה לאשת אח, שכן בידו לרבות? אחות אב ואם תוכיח. וחזר הדין: הצד השוה שבהן, שהן אסורות עליו משום ערוה ועשה בהן העראה כגמר ביאה — אף אני אביא כל העריות בדין הזה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:16:1.english: From a brother's wife and a father's and [mother's] sister - For when you refute [it]: What [comparison can be made] to a father's and mother's sister, which is [unique in that it is] a prohibition that comes on its own? A brother's wife proves [otherwise]. What [comparison can be made] to a brother's wife, which is [unique in that] it is in one's power to multiply [such prohibitions]? A father's and mother's sister prove [otherwise]. And the derivation repeats: The common denominator between them is that they are forbidden to him as forbidden relatives, and [Scripture] treated the initial stage of intercourse like the completion of intercourse in their cases — so too, I will include all forbidden relatives through this derivation.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:16:2.hebrew: שכן איסורן משום שאר - ותפשוט כל האסורות משום שאר, אבל אשת איש דלאו משום שאר, מנא תיתי:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:16:2.english: For their prohibition is because of kinship - And [thus] you would resolve [the case of] all [relations] prohibited because of kinship; however, a married woman, who is not [prohibited] because of kinship, from where would [her law] come?

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:18:1.hebrew: בחיי אוסרן - כל זמן שאדם חי והיא שופעת. וכן אשת אח, אין היתר בחיי אחיו, שאפילו הוא מגרשה אסורה לזה. אשת איש יש לה היתר בחייו על ידי גט:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:18:1.english: During the lifetime of the one that renders them prohibited - [In the case of a menstruating woman, she is prohibited] as long as a person is alive and she is discharging [blood]; and similarly, a brother's wife has no permissibility during his brother's lifetime, for even if he divorces her, she is forbidden to this [brother]. [By contrast,] a married woman has permissibility during his [i.e., her husband's] lifetime by means of a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:1:1.english: A sleeping [man] has not acquired - For a sleeping [person] is not of sound mind, and his acquisition is not a [valid] acquisition.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:1:2.english: In [the case of] one who was inserted - [Meaning] that he became erect [intending] for his wife, and fell from the roof and was inserted into his yevama.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:1:3.hebrew: חייב בד' דברים - בנזק וצער ורפוי ושבת, כדאמר בהחובל (ב"ק דף פה:): פצע תחת פצע, לרבות השוגג כמזיד ואונס כרצון. אבל בבושת לא, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:1:3.english: He is liable for four things - For injury, pain, medical expenses, and loss of livelihood, as it states in [the chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 85b): "Wound for wound" — [this comes] to include one who acts inadvertently like one who acts intentionally, and one who acts under duress like one who acts willingly. However, [he is] not [liable] for humiliation, as [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:1:4.english: And with his yevama, he has not acquired [her] - For he did not intend [to engage in] intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:2:1.english: Where he intended [to have intercourse] with his wife - And became erect for her.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:3:1.english: A mitzvah - That is to say, [the mitzvah is] through intercourse rather than through chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:4:1.english: If he wishes - [It is] a mitzva to perform levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:5:1.hebrew: ולקחה שלא כדרכה - לרבות שאם בא עליה שלא כדרכה, קנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:5:1.english: And take her — atypical [intercourse] - [This comes] to include [the case] that if he had intercourse with her in an atypical manner, he has acquired [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:6:1.english: We read: "in the place where he establishes a name."

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:7:1.english: Unless he intends [to come] to her for the sake of sexual intercourse - In general.

Rashi on Yevamot 54a:9:1.hebrew: נזק - שמין אותה כאילו היא שפחה נמכרת, כמה היתה יפה וכמה היא יפה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54a:9:1.english: Injury - They appraise her as if she were a maidservant being sold: how much she was worth [before] and how much she is worth [now].

Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:14:1.hebrew: שכן בידו לרבות - וא"ת: דבקדושין פרק האומר (דף סז:) בעי למילף כל העריות דלא תפסי בהו קידושין מאחות אשתו, וקאמר התם: "בשלמא כולהו אתיין"; והיכי אתיין? הא איכא למיפרך: מה לאחות אשה שכן בידו לרבות! וי"ל: דבלאו הכי פריך שפיר. א"נ: דדוקא באשת אח חשיב "יש בידו לרבות" לחומרא, שכן יש בידו לרבות איסור על אחרים; אבל מה שבידו לרבות על עצמו לא חשיב פירכא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:14:1.english: Since it is within his power to increase - And if you ask: In Kiddushin, chapter HaOmer (67b), [the Gemara] seeks to derive [regarding] all forbidden relatives (arayot) that betrothal does not take effect with them from [the case of] his wife's sister, and it says there: "Granted, all of them can be derived [from her]." But how can they be derived? Surely one can object: "What [comparison can be made] to a wife's sister, since it is within his power to increase [the number of forbidden women]?" And one can answer: Even without this [objection], [the Gemara there] raises a valid refutation. Alternatively: Specifically with regard to a brother's wife is "it is within his power to increase" considered a stringency, because it is within his power to increase a prohibition upon others; however, what is within his power to increase upon himself is not considered a refutation.

Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:15:1.hebrew: מה לאחות אב ואחות אם שכן איסור הבא מאליו - הקשה ריב"ן: דמאחות אב ואם נילף איסור הבא מאליו, ומאשת אח נילף היכא דעל ידי קידושין. וי"ל, דאשת איש לא אתי, כדפריך בסמוך: "מה להנך שכן שאר":
Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:15:1.english: "What [comparison can be made] to a father’s sister and a mother’s sister, which are a prohibition that comes on its own?" - Rivan asked: From a father’s sister and a mother’s sister we should derive a prohibition that comes on its own, and from a brother’s wife we should derive [a case] where [the prohibition comes] through betrothal. And one can answer that a married woman would not be derived [from them], as [the Gemara] objects immediately afterward: "What [comparison can be made] to these, which are blood relatives?"

Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:1:1.hebrew: ישן לא קנה - פי' בקונטרס משום דלא הוי בר דעת. וקשיא, דהא קטן, אע"ג דלא הוי בר דעת, הוה קונה אי לאו דמיעטיה קרא. אלא טעמא משום דלא איכוין לביאה כלל, והוי כמתכוין להטיח בכותל דבסמוך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:1:1.english: A sleeping [man] has not acquired [his yevama] - Rashi explained [that it is] because he is not mentally competent. And this is difficult, for a minor, even though he is not mentally competent, would acquire [his yevama] were it not that a verse excluded him. Rather, the reason [he does not acquire her] is because he did not intend for intercourse at all, and he is like one who intends to strike against a wall, [mentioned] immediately below:

Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:4:1.hebrew: וכי איצטריך קרא בין בשוגג כו' - וא"ת: והא איצטריך לאשמועינן ביאה ביבמה, דלא כתיב אלא הכא? וי"ל: דמלהקים לאחיו שם נפקא. וא"ת: והא אכתי איצטריך לג"ש דלקמן, "יבמה מנין? אתיא ביאה ביאה"! וי"ל: דביאה דחייבי לאוין מופנה, וה"ל מופנה מצד אחד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:4:1.english: "And when the verse is needed, [it is for] whether unwittingly, etc." - And if you will say: Isn't [this verse] needed to teach us [that acquisition is through] intercourse in the case of a yevama, as [intercourse] is not written [with regard to her] except here? And one can answer that it is derived from "to establish a name for his brother." And if you will say: Still, isn't it needed for the gezeira shava [cited] later [in the Gemara]: "From where [is it derived for] a yevama? It is derived [via] 'intercourse, intercourse'"? And one can answer that [the mention of] intercourse in [the context of] those liable for negative commandments is free [for exegesis], so it is free [mufneh] from one side.

Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:7:1.hebrew: דמכוין לה - לאו דוקא נקט דמכוין לה, דהא בסמוך אמר דנתכוון להטיח בבהמה והטיח ביבמתו — קנה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54a:7:1.english: That he intends for her - [Rav Yehuda] did not state "that he intends for her" in a strict sense, for shortly afterward [the Gemara] says that if he intended to have intercourse with an animal and [instead] had intercourse with his yevama, he has acquired [her].
